North Pole Elf CanteenThe Santa ClauseElf made cocoa. Just right.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersBocconcini snowman skewersMozzarella balls with tomato hats and basil scarves, drizzled with olive oilHow to make it300g bocconcini250g cherry tomatoes1 bunch basil1 tsp black peppercorns1 tbsp extra virgin olive oilCrack the peppercorns and halve the cherry tomatoes.Stack three bocconcini on each skewer and top with a half tomato as a hat.Press in peppercorn eyes, tie a basil leaf as a scarf and drizzle with olive oil.MainsTurkey done rightBrined turkey breast rolled with sage butter, stuffing, roast potatoes, gravyHow to make it1.5kg turkey breast60g butter1 bunch sage1 packet stuffing mix1kg potatoes300ml chicken stockBrine the turkey overnight in salted water in the fridge.Mix the butter with chopped sage, spread over the turkey and roll. Peel and chop the potatoes.Roast the turkey at 170°C until 70°C inside, with the potatoes in the tray for the last hour.Rest the turkey for 20 minutes. Bake the stuffing alongside as the packet says.Make gravy with the pan juices and stock.Christmas Eve diner pancake stackThe diner full of dads who burnt the turkeyHow to make itAs written, serves 4Fluffy buttermilk pancakes stacked with crisp bacon, fried eggs and golden hash browns, warm maple syrup and butter on top.Whisk 250g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 375ml buttermilk, 2 eggs and 40g melted butter and rest 15 minutes.Bake 8 frozen hash browns at 220°C for 20 minutes.Fry 8 rashers bacon until crisp.Cook ladles of batter in a buttered pan for 2 minutes a side.Fry 4 eggs.Stack 3 pancakes per plate with bacon, an egg and hash browns, then butter and maple syrup.SweetsNorth Pole gingerbreadSpiced gingerbread cut into elf shapesHow to make it125g butter100g brown sugar100g golden syrup300g plain flour2 tsp ground ginger1 tsp cinnamon1/2 tsp bicarb soda200g icing sugarred and green food colouring, a few drops of eachMelt the butter, sugar and golden syrup, then stir in the flour, ground ginger, cinnamon and bicarb.Chill the dough.Roll out and cut into elves and trees.Bake at 180°C until firm.Mix the icing sugar with a little water, tint red and green and ice the cooled biscuits.Santa's milk and cookiesBrown butter chocolate chip cookies, dough rested overnight for chewy centresHow to make it150g butter200g brown sugar1 egg250g plain flour1/2 tsp bicarb soda200g choc chips1 L full cream milkBrown the butter in a pan and leave to cool.Beat with the sugar and egg, then mix in the flour, bicarb and choc chips.Rest the dough overnight in the fridge.Shape into 16 cookies and bake at 180°C until golden at the edges.Serve with cold milk.DrinksJudy's cocoaCocoa made with milk and cream, cinnamon and vanilla, warmed to drinking heatHow to make it4 tbsp cocoa4 tbsp caster sugar1 pinch salt900ml full cream milk100ml thickened cream1 pinch cinnamon1 drop vanilla extractWhisk the cocoa, sugar and salt with a splash of the milk into a paste.Add the rest of the milk, cream, cinnamon and vanilla. Warm to drinking temperature without boiling.Pour into mugs.
